bug_description.normalized: The sample is admitted as an MDB database and reaches catalog row binding in `mdb_read_catalog()`. Catalog setup first stores heap-allocated destination buffers in the bound `MdbColumn::bind_ptr` fields for `MSysObjects`. A later fetched row is cracked into per-column metadata where a column can reach `_mdb_attempt_bind()` either with `isnull` set or with `siz == 0`; both source-level routes call `mdb_xfer_bound_data(..., len = 0)`. On that path `mdb_xfer_bound_data()` executes `strcpy(col->bind_ptr, "")`, and the saved ASan report records a SEGV caused by a READ from a wild high address at that exact line. The available staged artifacts prove the invalid pointer dereference at the sink, but they do not prove where the non-NULL invalid `bind_ptr` value originated after the earlier valid binding step.

source.value_from: Attacker-controlled MDB row bytes determine the null-mask bits and variable-column offsets used to materialize the field metadata later passed into the crashing bind path.
source.description: Row cracking is the first project statement on the witnessed path that consumes attacker-controlled row bytes into the vulnerability-relevant null-or-zero-length state used by `_mdb_attempt_bind()`.

root_cause.code: } else if (isnull) { mdb_xfer_bound_data(mdb, 0, col, 0); } ... else { mdb_xfer_bound_data(mdb, offset, col, len); }
root_cause.description: For non-boolean, non-OLE bound columns, `_mdb_attempt_bind()` routes both the null-field case and the zero-length field case into `mdb_xfer_bound_data()` with `len == 0`, selecting the sink path without any additional guard on the validity of the stored destination pointer.

sink.description: The empty-string transfer path dereferences `col->bind_ptr` at the exact line reported by ASan; the saved report says the crash is a READ from a wild high address during this `strcpy`.

parser_admitted.description: The sample is admitted far enough into MDB catalog parsing for `mdb_read_catalog()` to iterate `MSysObjects` rows.

tainted_value_origin.value_from: The row's null bitmap and variable-column offset table both come from attacker-controlled page bytes.
tainted_value_origin.description: Those row bytes control whether the later bind sees a null field or a zero-length field, the two source-level routes into `len == 0` at the sink path.

coarse_trace.summary: Catalog setup allocates output buffers and binds `MSysObjects` columns before row fetching begins.
Row cracking materializes per-column nullness and sizes from attacker-controlled row bytes.
The bind helper maps both null-field and zero-length field cases to `mdb_xfer_bound_data(..., len = 0)`.
The `len == 0` branch executes `strcpy(col->bind_ptr, "")`, where ASan reports a wild-address read.

fine_trace.note: For each cracked row field, attacker-controlled null-mask bits are converted into the `is_null` flag later passed to `_mdb_attempt_bind()`.

fine_trace.code: col_start = var_col_offsets[col->var_col_num]; fields[i].start = row_start + col_start; ... fields[i].siz = var_col_offsets[(col->var_col_num)+1] - col_start;
fine_trace.note: For variable columns, attacker-controlled row offsets are converted into the parsed start and size values; one source-grounded route to the sink is `fields[i].siz == 0`.

fine_trace.code: obj_id = malloc(mdb->bind_size); obj_name = malloc(mdb->bind_size); obj_type = malloc(mdb->bind_size); obj_flags = malloc(mdb->bind_size); obj_props = malloc(mdb->bind_size);
fine_trace.note: Catalog reading allocates heap buffers that are intended to receive bound `MSysObjects` column text.
Those catalog buffers are stored into the selected `MdbColumn` binding slots before any row is fetched, creating the destination-pointer state later consumed by row binding.

fine_trace.code: if (col->col_type == MDB_BOOL) { ... } else if (isnull) { mdb_xfer_bound_data(mdb, 0, col, 0); } else if (col->col_type == MDB_OLE) { ... } else { mdb_xfer_bound_data(mdb, offset, col, len); }
fine_trace.note: For the bound non-boolean, non-OLE column on the crashing path, `_mdb_attempt_bind()` forwards the parsed metadata and sends either the null-field case or the zero-length-field case into `mdb_xfer_bound_data()` with `len == 0`.

fine_trace.code: if (len) { col->cur_value_start = start; col->cur_value_len = len; } else { col->cur_value_start = 0; col->cur_value_len = 0; } if (col->bind_ptr) { if (!len) {
fine_trace.note: Inside the transfer helper, `len == 0` resets the current-value metadata and selects the empty-string copy subpath for the stored destination pointer.

The empty-string path dereferences `col->bind_ptr` at the exact crashing line; the saved ASan report identifies this as a READ from a wild high address, so the witnessed sink is an invalid-pointer dereference rather than a proven null dereference.

poc.trigger: Run the staged vulnerable `fuzz_mdb` target on the sample MDB until catalog parsing reaches a bound `MSysObjects` row and the bind helper invokes `mdb_xfer_bound_data()` on its `len == 0` path.

format.name: MDB catalog row
format.contract: The witness input must be an MDB file admitted into `mdb_read_catalog()` so that a fetched bound `MSysObjects` row reaches `_mdb_attempt_bind()` for a non-boolean, non-OLE column with either `isnull == 1` or `len == 0`. Both source-level alternatives force `mdb_xfer_bound_data(..., len = 0)`, which then executes `strcpy(col->bind_ptr, "")` at line 270. The saved artifacts do not prove a narrower predicate for how `col->bind_ptr` became the wild address observed by ASan.
